title: Torah permanence
thesis: No priesthood change abrogates the Torah; the Levitical order is suspended by the Temple's loss, not superseded.
alternative_reading: Psalm 110 addresses a Davidic king (or Abraham, in b. Nedarim 32b), whose priestly honour is not transferred to a later figure.

title: Israel-specific new covenant
thesis: The new covenant is addressed to Israel and Judah and its fulfilment for them is not exhausted by the church.
alternative_reading: Hebrews applies Jeremiah to the church by extension; Israel's covenantal identity persists (Romans 11:29).

title: Rhetorical silence
thesis: Hebrews 7:3 uses a known exegetical convention (quod non in thora non in mundo); it makes no claim about Melchizedek's nature.
alternative_reading: Read as Alexandrian-style argument from silence comparable to Philo, not as ontology.

title: Royal, not messianic-priestly
thesis: Psalm 110 is a royal enthronement psalm granting a Jerusalem king Melchizedek-like priestly prerogatives.
alternative_reading: The "priest forever" grants dynastic cultic rights to the Davidic king rather than predicting a future figure.
